q: Fluid can exert pressure by virtue of their _____.
e: A fluid presses on a surface because of its weight. Fluid can exert pressure by virtue of their weight. Volume or shape is not this quantity.

q: Fluid represents states of matter that take the _____ of their containers.
e: A fluid has no fixed shape. It takes the shape of the container. Solids do not. Shape is the term used with Fluid represents states matter that take.

q: Fluid is either liquid (or) _____.
e: The word fluid covers liquids and gases. Fluid is either liquid (or) gas. Solid or plasma is not this quantity.

q: The pressure exerted on a body by the atmosphere due to the weight of the atmosphere is called _____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The pressure exerted on a body by the atmosphere due to the weight of the atmosphere is called atmospheric pressure. Liquid pressure or gauge pressure is not this quantity.

q: At the earth's surface the magnitude of the atmospheric pressure is about _____.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². At the earth's surface the magnitude of the atmospheric pressure is about 100 kN m^-2. Do not trade 100 kN m^-2 for 10 kN m^-2 or 1000 kN m^-2.

q: We do not normally feel the large atmospheric pressure because the pressure inside our body is almost the same as the _____ and so balance it.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². We do not normally feel the large atmospheric pressure because the pressure inside our body is almost the same as the external pressure and so balance it. Internal pressure or blood pressure is not this quantity.

q: Nose bleeding which sometimes occurs at a place of low atmospheric pressure is due to the fact that the _____ is higher than the atmospheric pressure.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². Nose bleeding which sometimes occurs at a place of low atmospheric pressure is due to the fact that the blood pressure is higher than the atmospheric pressure. Do not trade blood pressure for air pressure or water pressure.

q: The atmospheric pressure at the plains is _____ than that at the hilly regions.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². The atmospheric pressure at the plains is higher than that at the hilly regions. Do not trade higher for lower or equal.

q: The atmospheric pressure changes according to locality and _____.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². The atmospheric pressure changes according to locality and time. Temperature or humidity is not this quantity.

q: The earth is surrounded by the atmosphere up to a height of several _____.
e: The atmosphere is a deep blanket of gas with weight, so it exerts pressure. The earth is surrounded by the atmosphere up to a height of several miles. Kilometres or metres is not this quantity.

q: The atmosphere consists largely of masses of gases and has _____.
e: The atmosphere consists largely of masses of gases and has weight. Do not trade weight for no mass or zero density.

q: The Italian scientist Evangelista Torricelli first noticed the variation of pressure due to height and _____.
e: Torricelli first tracked how air pressure changes with height and weather. The Italian scientist Evangelista Torricelli first noticed the variation of pressure due to height and time. Temperature or density is not this quantity.

q: Evangelista Torricelli invented and constructed a barometer in the year _____.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. Evangelista Torricelli invented and constructed a barometer in the year 1644. Do not trade 1644 for 1466 or 1544.

q: A barometer is a device for measuring _____.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. A barometer is a device for measuring atmospheric pressure. Liquid pressure or blood pressure is not this quantity.

q: The simple mercury barometer consists of a glass tube about _____ long sealed at one end and filled with mercury.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. The simple mercury barometer consists of a glass tube about 1 metre long sealed at one end and filled with mercury. 0.5 metre or 2 metres is not this quantity.

q: The atmospheric pressure in terms of height of mercury column in barometer is given by the formula _____.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². The atmospheric pressure in terms of height of mercury column in barometer is given by the formula p = ρ g h. p = ρ g / h or p = ρ / g h is a different relation from p = ρ g h.

q: The vertical height of the mercury column in a barometer depends only on the _____ outside the tube.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. The vertical height of the mercury column in a barometer depends only on the pressure outside the tube. Do not trade pressure for diameter or tilt.

q: The vertical height of the mercury column in a barometer does not depend on the _____ of the column.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. The vertical height of the mercury column in a barometer does not depend on the tilt of the column. Density or liquid is not this quantity.

q: The vertical height of the mercury column in a barometer is independent of the _____ of the tube.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. The vertical height of the mercury column in a barometer is independent of the diameter of the tube. Do not trade diameter for length or material.

q: Atmospheric pressure at sea level is known as the _____ atmospheric pressure.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². Atmospheric pressure at sea level is known as the standard atmospheric pressure. Do not trade standard for normal or absolute.

q: A pressure of $760 \text{ mm Hg}$ is known as standard atmospheric pressure or _____ atmosphere.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². A pressure of 760 mm Hg is known as standard atmospheric pressure or 1 atmosphere. Do not trade 1 for 2 or 0.5.

q: The density of mercury used in standard atmospheric pressure calculation is _____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². The density of mercury used in standard atmospheric pressure calculation is 13590 kg m^-3. Do not trade 13590 for 1000 or 1360.

q: $1 \text{ atm}$ is equal to _____ $\text{Pa}$.
e: 1 atm is equal to 1.013 × 10^5 Pa. 1.013 × 10^4 or 1.013 × 10^6 is a different relation from 1.013 × 10^5.

q: $1 \text{ atm}$ is equal to _____ $\text{hPa}$.
e: 1 atm is equal to 1013 hPa. Do not trade 1013 for 101.3 or 10130.

q: $1 \text{ atm}$ is equal to _____ $\text{bar}$.
e: 1 atm is equal to 1.01 bar. Do not trade 1.01 for 10.1 or 0.101.

q: $1 \text{ atm}$ is equal to _____ $\text{mmHg}$.
e: 1 atm is equal to 760 mmHg. Do not trade 760 for 76 or 7600.

q: In a drinking straw, the action of sucking increases the volume of the lungs, thereby _____ the air pressure in the lungs and the mouth.
e: Sucking lowers pressure in the mouth, so outside air pressure pushes the liquid up. In a drinking straw, the action of sucking increases the volume of the lungs, thereby reducing the air pressure in the lungs and the mouth. Increasing or maintaining is not this quantity.

q: When drawing a liquid into a syringe, the piston is pulled up and the pressure inside the cylinder _____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. When drawing a liquid into a syringe, the piston is pulled up and the pressure inside the cylinder decreases. Remains same or increases is not this quantity.

q: When pressing a rubber sucker on a smooth surface, most of the air inside is squeezed out and the pressure is _____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. When pressing a rubber sucker on a smooth surface, most of the air inside is squeezed out and the pressure is reduced. Zero or increased is not this quantity.

q: A rubber sucker is held in position by the _____ on its outside surface.
e: A rubber sucker is held in position by the atmospheric pressure on its outside surface. Do not trade atmospheric pressure for elastic force or liquid pressure.

q: The simple mercury barometer tube is inverted and the open end is submerged in a reservoir of _____.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. The simple mercury barometer tube is inverted and the open end is submerged in a reservoir of mercury. Water or oil is not this quantity.

q: The mercury column in a barometer is held up by the pressure of the atmosphere acting on the surface of mercury in the _____.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. The mercury column in a barometer is held up by the pressure of the atmosphere acting on the surface of mercury in the reservoir. Do not trade reservoir for tube or vacuum.

q: The space above the mercury column in a simple barometer is known as the _____ vacuum.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. The space above the mercury column in a simple barometer is known as the Torricellian vacuum. Partial or perfect is not this quantity.

q: If the tube of a barometer is lowered below 760 mm, the mercury would _____ fill the tube.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. If the tube of a barometer is lowered below 760 mm, the mercury would completely fill the tube. Do not trade completely for partially or not.

q: Standard atmospheric pressure is expressed as $14.7 \text{ lb in}^{-2}$, which is also known as _____.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². Standard atmospheric pressure is expressed as 14.7 lb in^-2, which is also known as psi. Atm or pa is not this quantity.

q: Standard atmospheric pressure is also equal to 760 _____.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². Standard atmospheric pressure is also equal to 760 torr. Pa or bar is not this quantity.

q: In a syringe, atmospheric pressure acting on the liquid drives the liquid into the cylinder through the _____.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². In a syringe, atmospheric pressure acting on the liquid drives the liquid into the cylinder through the nozzle. Do not trade nozzle for piston or handle.

q: A liquid exerts pressure because of its _____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. A liquid exerts pressure because of its weight. Do not trade weight for volume or shape.

q: The pressure exerted by a liquid depends on the _____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The pressure exerted by a liquid depends on the depth. Base area or container shape is not this quantity.

q: The pressure exerted by the liquid at the bottom surface is given by the formula _____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The pressure exerted by the liquid at the bottom surface is given by the formula p = ρ g h. p = ρ g / h or p = ρ / g h is a different relation from p = ρ g h.

q: The pressure exerted by the liquid is directly proportional to the height of the liquid and the _____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The pressure exerted by the liquid is directly proportional to the height of the liquid and the density. Do not trade density for base area or volume.

q: The pressure exerted by the liquid is independent of the _____ of the container.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The pressure exerted by the liquid is independent of the base area of the container. Depth or liquid density is not this quantity.

q: The true pressure at the depth $h$ in the liquid is given by the formula _____.
e: In a static liquid, pressure rises with depth as ρgh. The true pressure at the depth h in the liquid is given by the formula p = patm + ρ g h. p = patm - ρ g h or p = ρ g h - patm is a different relation from p = patm + ρ g h.

q: The deeper the point inside the liquid the _____ is the pressure at that point.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The deeper the point inside the liquid the greater is the pressure at that point. Do not trade greater for lower or same.

q: The pressure in a liquid at a particular point acts _____ in all directions.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The pressure in a liquid at a particular point acts equally in all directions. Partially or differently is not this quantity.

q: The pressure exerted on the bases of containers having the same height and same density liquid would be the _____ even though their weights and shapes are different.
e: Density is mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V. The pressure exerted on the bases of containers having the same height and same density liquid would be the same even though their weights and shapes are different. Different or zero is not this quantity.

q: Since the weight of liquid becomes greater as the depth increases, the pressure also _____ with depth.
e: In a static liquid, pressure rises with depth as ρgh. Since the weight of liquid becomes greater as the depth increases, the pressure also increases with depth. Do not trade increases for decreases or remains same.

q: Pressure at any point inside a liquid is the _____ in all directions.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. Pressure at any point inside a liquid is the same in all directions. Different or zero is not this quantity.

q: There will be pressure not only at the top of the immersed body but also upward pressure at the bottom and _____ pressures at the sides.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. There will be pressure not only at the top of the immersed body but also upward pressure at the bottom and lateral pressures at the sides. Do not trade lateral for downward or zero.

q: A glass tube open at both ends and bent into a _____ shape serves as a sensitive device for measuring pressure.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. A glass tube open at both ends and bent into a U shape serves as a sensitive device for measuring pressure. V or l is not this quantity.

q: A manometer is usually filled with coloured water, light oil, or _____.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. A manometer is usually filled with coloured water, light oil, or mercury. Do not trade mercury for alcohol or acid.

q: Manometers are very sensitive for measuring pressure differences, especially when the filling liquid is water or _____.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. Manometers are very sensitive for measuring pressure differences, especially when the filling liquid is water or light oil. Do not trade light oil for mercury or alcohol.

q: A manometer filled with _____ is not sensitive.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. A manometer filled with mercury is not sensitive. Do not trade mercury for water or light oil.

q: A sphygmomanometer which is used to measure blood pressure is a kind of _____-filled manometer.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. A sphygmomanometer which is used to measure blood pressure is a kind of mercury-filled manometer. Do not trade mercury for oil or water.

q: When both sides of the U-tube manometer are exposed to the atmosphere, the levels of the liquid in the two sides are the _____.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. When both sides of the U-tube manometer are exposed to the atmosphere, the levels of the liquid in the two sides are the same. Different or zero is not this quantity.

q: If the pressures on the two liquid columns of a manometer are different, the levels will _____.
e: A barometer reads atmospheric pressure. A manometer reads a pressure difference. If the pressures on the two liquid columns of a manometer are different, the levels will no longer be the same. Be the same or drop to zero is not this quantity.

q: When bodies are immersed in a liquid there is loss in weight due to a property of liquids called _____.
e: When bodies are immersed in a liquid there is loss in weight due to a property of liquids called buoyancy. Viscosity or surface tension is not this quantity.

q: Since buoyant force is directed upward, it is called _____.
e: Buoyant force is the upward push of the fluid, equal to the weight of the displaced fluid. Since buoyant force is directed upward, it is called upward thrust. Downward thrust or lateral thrust is not this quantity.

q: Archimedes' principle states that the upward thrust acting on a body which is immersed in a liquid is equal to the _____ of the liquid displaced by the body.
e: Archimedes' principle: the upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced. Archimedes' principle states that the upward thrust acting on a body which is immersed in a liquid is equal to the weight of the liquid displaced by the body. Volume or mass is not this quantity.

q: Archimedes' principle is true not only for liquids but also for _____.
e: Archimedes' principle: the upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced. Archimedes' principle is true not only for liquids but also for gases. Do not trade gases for solids or plasmas.

q: The weight of a body when it is immersed in a liquid is called _____ weight.
e: The weight of a body when it is immersed in a liquid is called apparent weight. Actual or true is not this quantity.

q: The apparent weight of a body is less than the actual weight because of the _____ of the liquid acting on it.
e: The apparent weight of a body is less than the actual weight because of the upward thrust of the liquid acting on it. Do not trade upward thrust for downward thrust or friction.

q: If the weight of the body is greater than the upward thrust, the body will _____.
e: If the weight of the body is greater than the upward thrust, the body will sink. Do not trade sink for float or rise.

q: If the weight of the body is smaller than the upward thrust, the body will rise up to the _____.
e: If the weight of the body is smaller than the upward thrust, the body will rise up to the surface. Do not trade surface for bottom or middle.

q: A body will float in a liquid if the upward thrust acting on it is equal to its _____.
e: A body will float in a liquid if the upward thrust acting on it is equal to its weight. Volume or density is not this quantity.

q: For a floating body, the ratio of the densities is equal to the ratio of the immersed volume to the volume of the _____.
e: For a floating body, the ratio of the densities is equal to the ratio of the immersed volume to the volume of the whole body. Displaced liquid or container is not this quantity.

q: The volume of a totally immersed block is equal to the volume of liquid _____ by the block.
e: The volume of a totally immersed block is equal to the volume of liquid displaced by the block. Do not trade displaced for absorbed or evaporated.

q: The forces acting on the sides of a totally immersed block _____.
e: The forces acting on the sides of a totally immersed block cancel out. Do not trade cancel out for add up or increase.

q: The net force acting on a totally immersed block in the upward direction is called the _____ force.
e: The net force acting on a totally immersed block in the upward direction is called the buoyant force. Gravitational or frictional is not this quantity.

q: The densities of various substances can be obtained by using _____ principle.
e: The densities of various substances can be obtained by using Archimedes' principle. Pascal's or bernoulli's is not this quantity.

q: If a body is in equilibrium while floating, the net force acting on it is _____.
e: If a body is in equilibrium while floating, the net force acting on it is zero. Maximum or minimum is not this quantity.

q: Any increase in pressure at the surface of an enclosed fluid must be transmitted to _____ in the fluid.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. Any increase in pressure at the surface of an enclosed fluid must be transmitted to every other point in the fluid. Do not trade every other point for the bottom only or the top only.

q: Pascal's law was first recognized by French scientist Blaise Pascal in the year _____.
e: Pressure is force over area. The SI unit is the pascal, N m⁻². Pascal's law was first recognized by French scientist Blaise Pascal in the year 1650. 1550 or 1750 is not this quantity.

q: When a fluid completely fills a vessel and a pressure is applied to it at any part of the surface, that pressure is transmitted _____ throughout the whole of the enclosed fluid.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. When a fluid completely fills a vessel and a pressure is applied to it at any part of the surface, that pressure is transmitted equally throughout the whole of the enclosed fluid. Partially or unequally is not this quantity.

q: The concept of Pascal's law is very useful in the working principle of hydraulic brakes and hydraulic _____.
e: Pressure is force over area. The SI unit is the pascal, N m⁻². The concept of Pascal's law is very useful in the working principle of hydraulic brakes and hydraulic presses. Do not trade presses for lifts or jacks.

q: Hydraulic brakes are used in cars and other _____.
e: Hydraulic brakes are used in cars and other vehicles. Airplanes or ships is not this quantity.

q: A hydraulic press is used for baling jute, hay, cotton and for shaping _____ and metal sheets.
e: A hydraulic press is used for baling jute, hay, cotton and for shaping steel and metal sheets. Do not trade steel for plastic or wood.

q: A hydraulic press is named a _____ multiplier.
e: A hydraulic press is named a force multiplier. Pressure or work is not this quantity.

q: Assuming there is no friction in the hydraulic press system, the work done by effort equals the work done by the _____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Assuming there is no friction in the hydraulic press system, the work done by effort equals the work done by the upward force. Do not trade upward force for downward force or friction force.

q: Another useful machine based on Pascal's law is a hydraulic _____.
e: Pressure is force over area. The SI unit is the pascal, N m⁻². Another useful machine based on Pascal's law is a hydraulic lift. Do not trade lift for press or brake.

q: By applying a small force on the small piston of a hydraulic lift, it produces a large upward force on the _____ piston.
e: By applying a small force on the small piston of a hydraulic lift, it produces a large upward force on the large piston. Do not trade large for small or medium.

q: When a fluid completely fills a vessel, a pressure applied to it at any part of the surface is transmitted equally throughout the whole of the _____ fluid.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. When a fluid completely fills a vessel, a pressure applied to it at any part of the surface is transmitted equally throughout the whole of the enclosed fluid. Do not trade enclosed for open or gaseous.

q: In a hydraulic press, the upward force $F_{out}$ on area $A_{out}$ is calculated using the formula $F_{out} = p_{in} \times$ _____.
e: In a hydraulic press, the upward force Fout on area Aout is calculated using the formula Fout = pin × Aout. Do not trade Aout for Ain or Atotal.

q: In a hydraulic press, the pressure $p_{in}$ obtained by applying effort is equal to the pressure $p_{out}$ according to _____ law.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. In a hydraulic press, the pressure pin obtained by applying effort is equal to the pressure pout according to Pascal's law. Do not trade Pascal's for Newton's or Archimedes'.
